Renton, Auburn, Kent and the refineries: SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410 for Seattle-area NDT work

Ask a dozen Puget Sound NDT technicians which document their certification sits under and you will hear both names. King and Pierce counties hold Boeing's 737 line in Renton, its specialty metal-parts plant in Auburn, the Frederickson composite plant near Tacoma that builds the 777X carbon-fiber tail, Blue Origin's headquarters in Kent, and hundreds of machine, finishing and composite shops that sell to them. The same region runs refinery turnarounds, ship repair at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard, and bridge and building steel. The scheme follows the work, not the zip code.

Which document usually applies, by type of employer

Where you workUsual basis for certificationWhy
Supplier making parts for an airframe or engine makerNAS 410, or EN 4179 on European ordersThe customer's purchase order or quality clause invokes it, and each tier passes it to whoever inspects the hardware
Space-hardware maker in Kent or RedmondWhatever its quality system and contracts nameSpace customers write their own requirements; ask which standard the written practice cites
FAA repair station or airline maintenance shopThe standard in the repair station manual and customer contractsThe FAA does not certify NDT personnel; AC 65-31B lists NAS 410, ATA Specification 105 and SNT-TC-1A among acceptable standards
Refinery, terminal or pressure-equipment contractorASNT SNT-TC-1A, or CP-189 where a code names itASME, API and AWS documents call for it
Navy ship repair contractorNAVSEA technical publications plus the contractNavy documents bring their own personnel qualification rules

From a turnaround crew to an aerospace shop

Plenty of technicians start on refinery work at Anacortes or the Tacoma tideflats and later apply to a shop in Auburn, Kent or Renton. An SNT-TC-1A certification does not travel; the new employer certifies you again under its own written practice. If that practice is built on NAS 410, its Responsible Level 3 (RL3) reviews your file and decides what earlier training and experience to credit. The old certificate is useful evidence, yet it never meets a NAS 410 requirement by itself.

The usual gap is in the surface methods. NAS 410 expects more formal, documented magnetic particle and penetrant training than SNT-TC-1A recommends, so a technician with years of field MT on welds may still owe classroom hours before an aerospace certification. Ultrasonic work on carbon-fiber laminate is another step up from weld UT; the aviation ultrasonic testing guide shows what changes.

Five questions for the hiring Level 3

  1. Which standard, and which revision, does your written practice certify me under?
  2. Will you credit my existing training hours, and do you need the course outlines to do it?
  3. How much supervised experience must I log in each method before examination?
  4. Who writes and grades the specific and practical examinations, and on which parts?
  5. If I leave, will I receive copies of my training, experience and examination records?

Keep your own copies regardless: outlines with hours, a signed experience log by method, examination history and your vision record. That file is what the next RL3 reads.

For supplier quality managers in King and Pierce counties

Many shops here ship aerospace parts in the morning and industrial work in the afternoon. If you run two programs, or one written practice with separate sections, put the standard and revision on every certification letter, keep training records to the stricter NAS 410 standard of evidence, and plan the move to Revision 6, released in December 2025, as customers call for it. Nadcap AC7114 auditors trace each technician from a signed report back to training, experience and examination records. Atlantis can help with NAS 410 audit documentation for Seattle-area suppliers: we prepare and review the files, and your RL3 approves them.

Where Atlantis fits in Seattle

Aerospace and aviation employers in Seattle get the same Atlantis offer as a refinery contractor or a fabricator. Training is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A: self-paced online theory with questions answered by our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT), practice in the Practical NDT simulator, and the hands-on work and practical examination at your employer's facility under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Seattle. For aerospace companies we write SNT-TC-1A-based written practices aligned to customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114, prepare procedures, administer Level I and II examinations and act as outside agency ASNT Level III. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3, in Seattle or anywhere else. Whether outside training counts toward a NAS 410 certification is your employer's RL3's call, so put the question to them before you enroll. The NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A comparison covers the two documents line by line, and the Everett page covers the Paine Field side of the region.
